title: F.P.Journe lineSport Centigraphe Reference CT2 in 18K Rose Gold Full Set New
description: The Centigraphe Sport CTS was produced from 2014 to 2018. Collectors love the Centigraphe Sport for the sport-oriented design with incredible versatility. This example is an incredible case and bracelet are made of 18k rose gold (6N) which is incredibly comfortable and elegant on the wrist. F.P.Journe collectors love these bracelets and they are among the best quality in the industry. The case and bracelet feature the “hammered” finish which is an attractive matte finish which is much more attractive than other manufacturers. The case measures approximately 42mm in diameter. The dial features non-luminous matte 5N Gold applied numerals. It features whitened guilloché subdials in silver with red accents. These grey dial variants were recently discontinued and transitioned to a black dial variant, making this one of the final grey variants. The movement is an engineering highlight. It is powered by the calibre 1506 - a movement which is made of titanium and weighs approximately 12 grams. The lineSport Centigraphe Reference CT2 is arguably one of the most advanced chronograph models ever produced capable of timing one-hundredth of a second. The subdials feature a 1/100th of a second at 10 o'clock, a 20 second dial, and a 10-minute dial at 6 o'clock. The watch comes full set from the original owner. It is in brand new condition. The watch was originally sold in 2024.

Starting in the 1970s, Rolex changed the dial to have Cellini instead of Midas in Greek on the dial and also introduced the smaller Queen Midas model. The King Midas has been closely associated with Elvis Presley, who is photographed holding one, and more recently with Rihanna, who wore a customized model for her pregnancy announcement. It is said that Gérald Genta designed these watches and they certainly seemed to be part of the evolution of integrated watch design that led to the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, IWC Ingenieur 1832, and Patek Philippe Nautilus. This example is 18k yellow gold. It is a fantastic timepiece. The case has been polished. The watch features a 3.7M serial dating to circa 1974. The bracelet can fit a wrist up to 7 inches The watch does not come with original Midas urn — as many examples have been damaged or lost over the decades. We have an example that is available for $19,000. It does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

Nobody was certain whether the watch was a hoax or an authentic release from The Crown. This “Puzzle” Day-Date in rose gold is in outstanding condition. It is an incredible off catalog Rolex. description: This is an incredibly special Patek Philippe reference 404 with a possibly unique dial featuring unusual hard enamel sector-like hour markers in the center of the dial resembling cat whiskers and what is perhaps the most outrageous and cool '7' even seen on a Patek Philippe. In fact, on close inspection, the '7' actually appears to be a modified upside-down '2' as seen in the '12'. Beyond the spectacular three-tone Art-Deco style dial and the beautiful curved long Patek Philippe & Co. signature on the dial is the engraving on the back commemorating the flight of the French seaplane the "Croix du Sud" from Cherbourg, France to Ziguinchor, Senegal. Lieutenant de vaisseau Henri-Laurent Dalliere, a French aviation legend, presumably purchased or was given this watch upon his return to France. The watch has "Fab. Suisse" on the bottom of the dial indicating it was likely originally designated to be sent to France by Patek Philippe among with a French gold hallmark on the case. This case is 18k yellow gold and measures approximately 20mm x 35mm in diameter. The rectangular dial features a subsidiary seconds at 6 o’clock and applied numerals at the 11, 12, 1, 5 and 7 o’ clock positions. It comes with an 18 yellow gold signed Patek Philippe buckle which is later. It comes with an extract from the Patek Philippe archives and was originally sold in 1935. This watch does not include the original box and papers, has a manual-wind movement (Caliber 9’’’90 made by Patek Philippe). We do not know the service history, but it is running well

title: Patek Philippe Ref 3520 in 18k YG Clous De Paris Unpolished Full Set
description: This is a beautiful and elegant Patek Philippe Calatrava reference 3520 in 18k yellow gold. It measures 32mm in diameter by 37mm in length. The case features a beautiful Clous De Paris texture. It features an 18k gold buckle. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch comes with a box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It was originally sold in 1989.

title: Patek Philippe “Hour Glass” Ref. 1593 in 18k Yellow Gold w/ Extract
description: This Patek Phillippe time only watch measures 25.5mm by 42mm and is made of 18k yellow gold. The reference 1593 features the sought after “hour glass” case shape. It is powered by the manually wound calibre 9””90 movement. It features a service dial which is printed. The watch does not come with a box and papers. It does come with an Extract from The Archives. It was originally sold on April 17th, 1948. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Ref 2508 in 18K YG Unpolished w/ Extract
description: The Patek Philippe reference 2508 is one of the most amazing time-only models. It is powered by the calibre 27 SC. This example, with an 18K yellow gold case, is in fantastic condition. It appears to be unpolished. It is 35mm in diameter and produced by François Borgel (Taubert Frères). The dial is features some marks, but is attractive and features non-luminous hour markers and hands. The watch comes with an Extract from The Archives. It does not come with a box. The watch was serviced by Patek Philippe in August 2025 and is running well. It was originally sold on January 26th, 1957. For those looking for an incredible mid-century Patek Philippe, this is a special watch.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Cartier Reference 3468 in 18K YG w/ Extract Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe reference 3468 is an interesting Calatrava model in 18k yellow gold. The watch features a blue sunburst dial, which is extra special due to the double-signed Cartier retailer signature. Double signed dials from Rolex and Patek Philippe are highly sought after. The case measures 33mm in diameter (39mm lug-to-lug). It is made of 18k yellow gold. The caseback features an incredible engraving. It is paired on a Cartier leather strap with 18k yellow gold deployant buckle. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with box and papers. It does come with an Extract from the Archives and was originally sold in 1969. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Calatrava Reference 5120G-001 in White Gold Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe Calatrava reference 5210 is a fantastic dress watch. The white gold case measures 35mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. It features a beautiful Clous de Paris bezel with white dial. The watch is powered by the microrotor calibre 240/111. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. We do now knot he date of production.

title: Patek Philippe Ref. 4972 Diamonds in 18k White Gold Full Set Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe reference 4972/1G-001 is an elegant timepiece with a radical case design. Patek Philippe is very traditional, yet the manufacturer has a great catalog of asymmetrical case designs. The case is 18k white gold. It features a white mother of pearl guilloché dial. It is powered by a quartz movement. The case measures approximately 39mm by 27mm at the widest points. The case features beautiful pavé set diamonds. The watch comes with a box and papers. It was originally sold in 2022. We do not know the service history, but it is running well and keeping good time.

title: Patek Philippe Ref 783 “Montres Golf” Retailed By Gübelin Designed by Gilbert Albert w/ Pouch & Extract Unpolished
description: The watch is uniquely stylish and it is quite apparent when looking at certain elements, such as the segmented dial, that it was created by the designer. The watch is powered by the calibre 12-400, and the case measures 39mm in diameter and 8mm in height (including the crystal). In addition, it is a double-signed dial sold by the Lucerne-based retailer Gübelin. The case back features the Poinçon de Maître key numbered 2 indicating F. Baumgartner SA, a case specialist who produced the cases many water-resistant Calatrava wristwatches, including the legendary reference 2526. While many collectors prioritize wristwatches, this pocket watch is a treasure and an absolutely mesmerizing creation from one of the watch industry’s most talented minds. This particular model is from the “Montres Golf” collection of three different models depicted in the advertisement (reference 782, reference 783, and reference 799) with integrated chains made for golfers to have in their pocket when playing golf. These golf watches became somewhat in vogue in the mid-20th century as golf became more popular and it became more widely-known that the impact of a swing could damage a wristwatch’s movement. The integrated chain allowed the golfer to clip it to their pocket for quick access to the time when on the course and also to ensure that it would not accidentally get lost. The “Montres Golf” watches also frequently came with a brown leather pouch, sometimes embossed with PATEK PHILIPPE in gold, but in the case of this watch embossed with GÜBELIN in gold. This reference 783 has an ornate wreath-like pattern on the chain and edge of the case that makes it particularly appealing. This watch came from the grandson of the original owner, who was a diplomat for Iran in the 1950s and 1960s, before the Shah was deposed, and likely was a gift to him by another diplomat. title: Patek Philippe Reference 785 Retailed by Beyer w/ Extract Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe reference 785 is a very rare pocket watch with incredibly ornate details. It features a Florentine bezel accented with a refined rope chain on both the chain and fob. The watch features the segmented dial found in many of the Patek Philippe timepieces by the highly important designer Gilbert Albert, The watch was most likely designed by Albert and dates to the 1960s. It is paired on a pinned rope and is intended to be worn as a brooch. The case is unpolished. The dial is original and unrestored. It is very similar to the reference 799 as one of the Montres Golf watches . According to Tortella and Sons, there are only 5 examples known and this appears to be the 6th example known. The watch does not come with box and papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives from Patek Philippe and Beyer.

title: Richard Mille RM 36-01 G-Sensor Tourbillon Sébastien Loeb w/ Box & Papers
description: The manufacturer is one of the most innovative manufacturers known for their use of lightweight and durable case materials most notably carbon TPT and titanium. Their distinct design language utilizes the tonneau case design with open work movements. French rally driver Sébastien Loeb is widely considered one of the best ever to compete in the World Rally Championship, boasting an unmatched record of 9 consecutive championship victories. In a limited edition of 30 pieces, the RM 36-01 was designed specifically with racing in mind. The Calibre 36-01 features a G-sensor which indicates up to 6 G’s of force. The titanium case measures 47.7mm in diameter. The strap is designed with carbon nanotubes and the movement features parts made with grade 5 titanium, black PVD, treated movement parts. The watch comes from the original owner. It was purchased in January of 2022. It comes with box and papers.

title: Cartier Tank Louis Xl Jumbo 17002 in 18K White Gold Unpolished
description: The Cartier Tank Louis is one of the most sophisticated dress watches and these models have grown to become highly collectible over recent years. It is a great contrast to many sports Rolex models within a collection and can be worn in both a casual and dressed up state. This example dates to the 1970s. It features an 18K white gold case which is extremely rare. These are the largest vintage Cartier Tank models. The case measures 28mm in diameter and 35mm in length. It appears to be unpolished. The dial appears to be a service dial with SWISS at 6 o'clock. It is powered by the automatic calibre 170. This is an interesting model also worn by David Prowse (the famous actor who played Darth Vader in the Stars Wars Trilogy). Prowse owned a yellow gold example from the era. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. It comes with a Cartier strap that is very short. It also comes with a white-gold Cartier deployant buckle.

title: Cartier Santos-Dumont Skeleton WHSA0044 Full Set Brand New
description: This Cartier Santos-Dumont is a micro-rotor skeleton watch, in large size, with a stainless steel case. The micro-rotor powers the automatic caliber 9629 MC. The black lacquer and steel case measures 43.5 mm x 31.4 mm and is 8mm thick. The watch is paired with a Cartier black alligator leather strap with steel signed buckle. The watch is brand new. The current retail price for this watch is $35,300. The watch comes as a “full set” with a box, papers and an additional strap. It was originally sold in 2025. description: This is a sophisticated Cartier Santos Dumont two tone time only dress watch. This reference WGSA0032 features a beautiful grey dial with Roman numerals. The watch comes with a box and papers. It was originally sold in 2025. We do not know the extent of the service history, but the watch is running well.

description: This is an uncommon Memovox model - a reference E 850. The cases on these are super cool and measure 33.5mm in diameter. These references were produced in the 50s, but we believe this example may have been assembled and sold in the 1960s with a tritium dial and signed crowns. The watch does not include box and papers. The watch was just serviced and is running well. It comes with Extract from The Archives.

title: Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox E 855 in 18K YG on Bracelet w/ Box
description: The reference’s “E” stands for Etanche, which indicates the case is a water-resistant model. The Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox reference E 855 is one of my favorite watches of all time. This example dates to mid 1960s. The case measures 37mm in diameter and wears excellent. The 18k yellow gold case has been lightly polished. It is paired on the impossible-to-find 18k yellow gold Jaeger-LeCoultre Gay Freres bracelet. It features the uncommon baton hands instead of of “fork” or dauphine hands. These are seen in catalogs from the 1960s. The watch is powered by the calibre 825, the first automatic alarm wristwatch to incorporate the calendar complication. The movement is a bumper-automatic, which means it does not rotate a full 360 degrees. Instead, the oscillating weight will bounce back and forth between two spring sides within the movement. The watch does not come with papers. It comes with a beautiful LeCoultre box which was likely added later. We do not know the service history but it is running well. To learn more about this model, read Charlie Dunne’s Coll ector's Guide: Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox Reference E 855 .

title: Zenith El Primero Ref A386 on Gay Freres Bracelet Unpolished
description: Introduced in 1969, the Zenith El Primero Reference A386 sits amongst the most celebrated chronographs in watchmaking. Powered by the automatic high-beat calibre 3019, the highly emphasized red chronograph hand glides over the dial in the smoothest manner. The model’s hands and hour markers feature a pale yellow tritium that immediately catches the attention of the wearer. Competing with the tri-colored subdials, the attributes of this watch are really a beautiful testament to the sports watches of yesteryear. This particular example comes with the Gay Frères steel ladder bracelet dating to 1969. The watch is 38mm wide (with a lug-to-lug length of 45.5mm). title: Abercrombie & Fitch Seafarer Ref 2443 Unpolished
description: The most desirable models from the retailer would be the Seafarer. This reference 2443 is the first of two variants with the “psychedelic” tidal register in graduated colors. variant. It is much more similar to the Seafarer reference 346. The later version had more of a Tiffany blue color in the minute register and the tidal register was both that Tiffany blue color and yellow rather than graduated colors. All of these early Seafarer models are extremely rare. The watch features a Valjoux 72 movement which was modified to incorporate a tide complication. The case appears to be unpolished. This Seafarer has a steel case and measures in at 38mm wide. The bottom right lug is bent from an impact. The dial is weathered, but appears to be original. It is paired on a contemporary beads of rice bracelet. The lume in the hands has been redone. The watch does not come with box and papers. It was recently services and is running well.

The watch does not come with a box and papers. The service history is unknown, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Jo Siffert Mk 2 Autavia Reference 1163 on GF Bracelet Unpolished
description: The Heuer “Jo Siffert” Autavia reference 1163 is one of the most iconic and exciting vintage Heuer chronographs. The watch was famously worn by the Swiss Formula 1 driver Jo Siffert in the late 1960s - early 1970s. This example dates to circa 1969. It is in outstanding condition. The case appears to be unpolished. It is powered by the automatic calibre 11 made by Heuer-Léonidas. It measures approximately 42mm in diameter. It features the Mark 2 dial and the original Tachymeter bezel. This variant has the enlarged blue hour markers and ridged hour markers and metal hour and minute hands. It features a 141XXX serial just after the Chronomatic Siffert range. It is paired on a Heuer bracelet by Gay Freres with HLD end links dating to 1970. For those looking for an incredible vintage Heuer chronograph, the Jo Siffert is a must have. This watch does not include the original box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Heuer Mk 6 Jo Siffert Autavia Ref 1163 Unpolished

title: HEUER Audi Sport Chronograph Unpolished
description: The Heuer Audi Sport chronographs are interesting stainless steel sport watches made initially for the UK market with a short production window dating to the 1980’s. The watch is powered by the Lemania 5100. The watch features a luminous black dial. There is a date window at 3 o’clock and it features a 12 hour elapsed time sup dial, and an orange elapsed time minute hand. The case appears to be unpolished. It does not come with a box or papers. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well.

title: Heuer Dato Carrera Reference 3147N Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s, the present watch is notably a “first execution” and features an unpolished case. Finding Carreras from the 1960s with in great condition is extremely difficult. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147N with the N meaning “Noir” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 189 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case diameter is 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. The present example is a bit of a hodgepodge. The watch features service replacement hands with Super-LumiNova. The case has been lightly polished and it has a replacement crystal. The case back sticker is in tact. It is possible the dial was placed in the watch. Regardless, it is a very rare dial and highly coveted vintage Heuer. An Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: Heuer Dato Carrera Ref. 3147S Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500 Unpolished
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147S with the S meaning “Silver” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 148 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case appears to be unpolished. The diameter measures approximately 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. We are not sure of the provenance of the watch, but it is an unbelievably attractive example. title: Urwerk UR-106 ‘Only Watch’ Full Set Mint Condition

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA In 18K YG
description: A Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA in 18K YG OMEGA introduced the Speedmaster in 1957, initially created for drivers in automotive racing needing to time their laps. However, the Speedmaster would reach eternal iconic status by eventually being qualified for spaceflight by NASA after an intense testing of several of the highest-grade chronographs of the 1960s. NASA selected the Speedmaster as the exclusive watch for use by its astronauts. The OMEGA Speedmaster reference 145.022-69 BA was the first OMEGA Speedmaster to be produced in 18k yellow gold. Only 30 examples were produced in total for astronauts and two were produced for President Nixon and Vice President Agnew. The next examples were given to Astronauts and are considered by many to be the grail OMEGA Speedmasters. On October 20, 2022, Wally Schirra’s personal OMEGA Speedmaster Professional BA 145.022 was sold for $1,906,954 . This example is one that was sold to the public. The 18K yellow-gold case is in has been lightly polshed. The dial is fantastic and the bezel remains in good condition. The watch is powered by the caliber 861. The bracelet is long and should fit a wrist approximately 7.1 inches. Finding an example with a long bracelet is incredibly difficult. For those looking for an epic gold Speedmaster, these are amazing watches. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ video and read the corresponding article. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do now know the service history, but it is running well.

This is an incredible “Racing Dial” reference 145.022-69. The watch was originally delivered to Japan in 1971 and was sold in 1975 according to the papers. title: Heuer USS Whale Carrera Reference 2447S Eggshell Dial
description: This annual watch prize tradition started in 1938 and continues to this day. L.Y. Spear, President of the Electric Boat Company (which became General Dynamics), started the Spear Foundation in 1942 with an endowment to fund the watch prize. The Spear Foundation allowed the shipmate to pick out his own watch from Mallove’s Jewelers in Groton, Connecticut. Brooks wisely selected a Carrera chronograph, but there was a catch. Navy regulations restricted external radioactive sources aboard nuclear-powered boats, so as to ensure accurate monitoring of radiation levels from propulsion systems. This watch had its tritium luminous material removed from dial and hands. An early dial was evidently selected for this purpose. This was possibly done on special order from Heuer, or by the retailer at the time of original sale. Brooks served a distinguished Navy career, including as Commander of the Sturgeon-class nuclear-powered attack submarine USS Whale (SSN-638) from 1975 to 1978, retiring with the rank of Captain. As a civilian, Brooks held important Senate-confirmed positions in government. He was appointed Ambassador to lead negotiation of two strategic arms reduction treaties between the U.S. and Russia, and served as U.S. Undersecretary of Energy for Nuclear Security, responsible for managing the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). The watch is powered by the Valjoux calibre 72. The case is lightly polished but very strong. The dial and hands had the original tritium luminous material removed. The signed crown is original. The watch is fitted on a black leather rally strap from Abel Court with a rare signed vintage “Sun” buckle. The watch does not come with box and papers. The watch will be accompanied by military ephemera personally owned by Ambassador Brooks – a framed photograph of USS Whale (SSN-638) during her sea trials, a heavy bronze insignia removed from the Whale and mounted on a wood plaque for presentation to Brooks, and selected books from Brooks’

O'Connor who worked at Jewel Tea Company. O’Connor was a respected executive at the company and within the U.S. coffee and tea industry throughout the mid-20th century. John F. McKieran, President of the National Coffee Association was quoted about O'Connor’s work stating “Jim O'Connor’s record as a coffee man goes back through so many years and covers so many outstanding achievements that it is almost superfluous for one to emphasize them. This is one of the most attractive Rolex Patrizzi Daytonas we have ever come across. It features a rich dark color on the outer ring of the registers. Rolex register rings on Daytonas with black dials from the early through middle 1990s sometimes would develop a darker tone in the subdials. This effect is often given the nickname “Patrizzi” after the legendary auctioneer Osvaldo Patrizzi, who reportedly first identified this patina. The present example is an outstanding example. It features a S serial number which dates to circa 1993. The watch comes with a reference 78390 Oyster bracelet with polished center links dating to circa 1995. title: Rolex Meters First Submariner Reference 5512 Unpolished w/ Box

It is was paired on a 7205 Rolex rivet bracelet with 80 end links dating to 1968. According to Rolex, the Submariner reference 5512’s production consisted of only 17,338 examples. The Submariner reference 5513’s production consisted of a much larger amount, 151,449 examples! Both Eric and I were quite astonished at the number of 5512 Submariners produced being a mere 17,338, as we assumed it was much larger - in the tens of thousands. In simplified terms, there was only just about one 5512 produced for every ten 5513s produced (or 11.4% specifically). It is extremely rare to find a great Submariner reference 5512. title: Rolex Domino's Air-King 14000 Full Set W/ Hangtag Unpolished
description: The Rolex-Domino’s connection is perhaps the ultimate high-low collaboration. These watches were not made for purchase by the public, but as a way to reward Domino’s franchise owners who hit their sales targets. All these watches were originally ordered through Schlanderer and Sons in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where Domino’s has its headquarters. In the past, these watches on the secondhand market were generally the least expensive Rolex a person could purchase as few people wanted a pizza logo like this on their dial. Dealers would buy them, swap out the Domino’s dial, and polish off the case back initials. Over the last year, however, they have gained a massive following. The watch features an engraving on the back with the recipient’s initials. You can learn about these watches in our video Collector Conversation: Tom Monaghan - Founder of Domino's Pizza - on the Domino's Rolex . This version features the “tilted logo” that is the last version of Dominos’s Rolex watch with the logo on the dial. . The watch features a U^ serial dating to 1997.
